title: [recordings] Recordings: upload, attach to event, quick transcript row, parts, state, playback and deletion — epic
body:
## Behavior specification

Recordings: upload, attach to event, quick transcript row, parts, state, playback and deletion.

This batch was planned from the reviewed design of the iOS app: every issue below states the backend behavior the app needs that `develop` does not provide yet. The issues are linked as sub-issues; their order follows the dependency graph across all batches, foundations first.

Status: drafts awaiting the `/define-behavior` Phase 5 audit. No issue in this batch carries `spec:approved` or `agent:ready` yet.

## Decisions

Decisions adopted while drafting, and questions still open for the product owner (per chunk of the batch):

### Decisions: recordings-1

#### (a) Decisions adopted
- Combined summary over all parts of an event? -> Decided by the product owner: no; in v1 each part has its own summary. A combined summary of a meeting may come later as notes on the Event. (#1464)
- "Done" signal variant (notification kind transcript_ready vs. Inbox badge only)? -> Decided by the product owner: the Inbox badge only; a push notification would interrupt needlessly. No done notification is built.
- Short-lived signed playback link? -> Decided by the product owner: not added; the local cache is enough, and a signed link is added only when a real problem shows up. The client uses the authenticated blob route with a local cache. (#1577)
- POST /api/transcriptions? -> Decided by the product owner: it stays out of scope. (#1574)
- Dedup upload of an existing recording with X-Event-Id and no event edge on its transcript -> link it to that event in the intake transaction; different event -> 409 recording_linked_elsewhere -> keeps repeated uploads safe and avoids silent relinking.
- Trashed event at upload time -> treated as no event, matching runs (design note acceptance criterion).
- recording_requests.event_decision -> default 'none', no CHECK constraint here; #1986 defines more values.
- Notification link for failed transcription -> ?page=transcript&id=<transcriptId>.
- Error code set -> budgetExceeded, mediaUnreadable, providerFailed, unknown, deleted (deleted written by #1582).

#### (b) Open questions for the product owner
- None remaining for this chunk.

#### (c) User-visible behavior
A recording made or imported next to an event (audio or video, with the time it was recorded) is uploaded in one call and attached to that event right away; a new "processing" row appears within seconds even while another long recording is being transcribed. An event can hold several recordings (parts) and a second recording in its time window joins it automatically. Failed transcriptions carry a stable reason and a notification that opens the transcript; transcripts carry their duration and finish time, can be played back in the app on the same timeline as the text, and are listed in a light list with their pairing state (linked to an event, waiting in the Inbox, none, processing), filterable by event, person and project, with per-day counts for the journal.


### Decisions: recordings-2

#### (a) Decisions adopted
- Does a finished transcript without an event get an AI title, or only "Recording D. M. HH:MM"? -> Decided by the product owner: as a proposal; after transcription Semp proposes a name on the recording's card and the user can edit it; until it is confirmed the recording is shown as "Recording D. M. HH:MM". Chain: user name, event name, then "Recording D. M. HH:MM"; the generated title is returned as `suggestedName`. (#1830)
- Placeholder during processing and for imports -> Decided by the product owner: neither "Dictaphone - import" nor "New recording"; an import gets the same pattern as every other recording, "Recording D. M. HH:MM". (#1830)
- Transcripts name may be empty? -> Decided by the product owner: yes; a transcript takes its title from its event or its recording date, so an empty stored name is fine; the non-empty title rule applies to the other collections. (#1830)
- May a recording at an event be named differently from the event? -> Yes, an own `name` takes precedence -> design note rule 1.
- Project chosen on the recording card vs. the event's project -> Decided by the product owner: the explicitly chosen project is an own value and linking the event does not overwrite it; the event's project is taken over only into an empty property. (#1696, #1697)
- Deleting a recording before the design includes it -> Decided by the product owner: not offered in the app until the design exists; then it goes through the generic Trash with restore, so the dedicated restore route is dropped and restoring the transcript from the Trash restores its source file too. (#1642)
- Transcript edge to a trashed event -> ignored by the match, replaced when linking elsewhere; generic edge PUT still answers cardinality_violation -> design note says so until an explicit assign action exists.
- Pipeline on deleted item -> clean stop, item_automation error with code deleted, no notification, job succeeds -> design note point 4.

#### (b) Open questions for the product owner
- None remaining for this chunk.

#### (c) User-visible behavior
A recording shows a meaningful title (the event name or "Recording 14. 10. 13:52") instead of its filename, and after transcription Semp proposes a generated name the user can edit and confirm. The language and the number of speakers chosen on the recording card are used for the transcription, and a project chosen there is on the transcript. Deleting an event leaves the recording's project and people as its own values and lets the recording be attached to another event; deleting a recording stops its processing without errors or notifications, a deleted recording is restored from the Trash together with its source file, and removing it for good also removes its processed audio files.



## Not planned yet

These pieces wait for a product decision and have no issue:

- Add the transcript_ready notification kind (decided: not in v1)
